- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early in horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp spike in true price (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days — apply a downward correction of 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the first 3–5 days of a new 30-day horizon — adjust upward by 1–3% based on recent 7-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model tends to lag — add a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.  
- When true price exceeds 75 in 3–5 days, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a 1–3% downward bias in later days of forecast.  
- If sentiment is negative and true price is rising, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment mismatch” error.
